title: Whose car has been driven more, Ravi's or Sheetal's?
description: Two cars show their distance on the dial. The video compares the two five digit numbers from the left, one place at a time.
teaching_notes: One idea: when both numbers have the same number of digits, compare from the left and stop at the first place that differs. Watch for comparing the ones digits first.

source: Let Us Do (second set) 3, the two cars
video_script.why: The child can compare numbers of different lengths but needs a method for two numbers of the same length.
video_script.substitution: Compare the ten thousands digits first, and look at later places only if they match.
video_script.anchor: two cars at a garage with distance dials showing how far each has gone
video_script.wrong_answer: ravi's car has been driven more, because seven is greater than three
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu compares the ones digits, seven and three, and says Ravi's car has been driven more. The ones place matters least, and the ten thousands place decides.
video_script.payoff_line: Sheetal's car has been driven more

final_answer.value: Sheetal's car, 67,543 km, has been driven more
final_answer.spoken: Sheetal's car, sixty-seven thousand five hundred and forty-three kilometres, has been driven more

hold_back: Sheetal's car, 67,543 km, has been driven more
never_show: Ravi's car marked as driven more
maths_rules: Ravi's car: 56,987 km; Sheetal's car: 67,543 km; both have 5 digits
slip: ones digits 7 and 3; 7 > 3 would suggest 56,987 is greater, but the ones place is the least important place and the ten thousands place decides
answer: Sheetal's car, 67,543 km, has been driven more
video_script.design: Exercise: compare two five digit numbers. Hint: both have five digits, so start at the left. The two dials stay on the stage and the digits are lit one place at a time.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a garage with two cars; Ravi's car dial marked 56,987 km and Sheetal's car dial marked 67,543 km; a question mark between the cars

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.garage: a garage appears with two cars
marks.ask: a question mark appears between the cars

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='garage'/>Two cars stand at a garage. Each has a dial that shows how far it has gone.
<bookmark mark='ravi'/>Ravi's car has been driven for fifty-six thousand, nine hundred and eighty-seven kilometres.
<bookmark mark='sheetal'/>Sheetal's car has been driven for sixty-seven thousand, five hundred and forty-three kilometres.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Whose car has been driven more?

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still and gets an accent underline

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: the two dials sit side by side; both digit rows glow and a count of five digits is written under each; a bar below reads which place to look at first; the first place of each pulses

marks.look: the digits of both dials glow
marks.need: the words start from the left appear
marks.try: the leftmost digit of each dial pulses

narration: <bookmark mark='look'/>Count the digits in each dial reading.
<bookmark mark='need'/>Both have the same number of digits, so start from the left.
<bookmark mark='try'/>Which place do you look at first? Try again with this.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows 7 greater than 3; the ones digits 7 and 3 are circled; the ten thousands digits 5 and 6 are left plain; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.chintu: Chintu's bubble appears with 7 greater than 3
marks.ones: the ones digits 7 and 3 are circled
marks.strike: the ten thousands digits glow and the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Ravi's car has been driven more, because seven is greater than three.
<bookmark mark='ones'/>He looked at the ones digits of the two dials.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>The ones place changes the number the least. The biggest place on the left decides first.

beats.on_screen: the ten thousands digits 5 and 6 glow; 6 > 5 is written; 67,543 > 56,987 is written

marks.tth: the ten thousands digits 5 and 6 glow

narration: <bookmark mark='tth'/>Look at the ten thousands place on both dials. Ravi's car shows five, and Sheetal's car shows six.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Six is greater than five, so we can stop here.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Sixty-seven thousand, five hundred and forty-three is greater than fifty-six thousand, nine hundred and eighty-seven.

beats.on_screen: Sheetal's car glows; the answer card shows Sheetal's car, 67,543 km, has been driven more
narration: <bookmark mark='who'/>Sheetal's dial has the greater number.
<bookmark mark='pay2'/>Sheetal's car has been driven more, by a margin that the ten thousands place settles.

beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the garage; two lines appear: same digits, start from the left; stop at the first place that differs; the two dials sit with the deciding digits circled

marks.cmp: the line start from the left appears
marks.rule: the line stop at the first place that differs appears
marks.ask: the deciding digits of both dials are circled

narration: <bookmark mark='cmp'/>To check, start from the left of both numbers.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Stop at the first place where the digits differ. The greater digit belongs to the greater number.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Is the digit you stopped at greater in the car you chose?
